Showing good sense and careful judgement — Juicioso/a / sensato/a.
A judicious choice saved them money.
Feel or express deep sorrow — Lamentar / llorar.
She lamented the loss of the old theatre.
An expression of grief — Lamento / elegía.
He sang a lament for the dead.
A heavy lack of energy — Letargo / apatía.
The heat brought on a general lethargy.
Clear and easy to understand — Claro/a / lúcido/a.
He had a lucid moment before sleeping.
Noun: lucidity. Phrase: a lucid dream.
Bringing in a lot of money — Lucrativo/a / rentable.
Related: lucre, meaning money, usually critical.
So silly it is laughable — Ridículo/a / absurdo/a.
Generous and forgiving, especially to a rival — Magnánimo/a.
Wanting to do harm — Malévolo/a / malintencionado/a.
Help two sides reach an agreement — Mediar / intermediar.
A neighbour mediated between the families.
v|Noun: mediation, mediator. Careful: mediate is to help, meditate is to think quietly.
Describing one thing as if it were another — Metáfora.
Time is money is a metaphor.
Adjective: metaphorical. Compare simile, which uses like or as.
Extremely careful about small details — Meticuloso/a / minucioso/a.
Ready to use strong or forceful methods — Militante / combativo/a.
A militant group blocked the road.
Noun: militancy. Also a noun: a militant.
Too interested in death or unpleasant things — Morboso/a.
He has a morbid curiosity about crashes.
She escapes the mundane by reading.
Also means of this world, as opposed to spiritual.
They were up to some nefarious scheme.
An opponent who cannot be beaten — Némesis / rival implacable.
The champion met his nemesis in the final.
A punishment that is deserved — Castigo merecido.
Greed proved to be his nemesis.
Plural: nemeses. From the Greek goddess of retribution.
Person who moves from place to place instead of settling — Nómada.
Calm and showing no concern — Despreocupado/a / indiferente.
A fond longing for the past — Nostalgia / añoranza.
Old songs fill him with nostalgia.
Adjective: nostalgic. Pattern: nostalgia for something.
The state of being completely forgotten — Olvido.
Being unaware of what is happening — Inconsciencia.
No longer used or useful — Obsoleto/a / en desuso.
Verb: obsolesce is rare; say become obsolete.
Extremely unpleasant; deserving hatred — Odioso/a / detestable.
Noun: odium. Related: odor is different, that is a smell.
Noun: omnipotence. Related: omniscient, knowing everything.
The duty or responsibility for something — Responsabilidad / carga.
The onus is on the seller to prove it.
Almost always in the onus is on someone.
Stated as the reason, though not the real one — Aparente / supuesto/a.
Adverb: ostensibly. Careful: ostensible is apparent, ostentatious is showy.
Something that is supposed to cure everything — Panacea.
Usually used to say something is not one.
A statement that seems to contradict itself but may be true — Paradoja.
It is a paradox that the more we have, the less we enjoy.
Person rejected by everyone — Paria / marginado/a.
He became a pariah after the scandal.
Extremely unwilling to spend — Mezquino/a / tacaño/a.
Their parsimonious host served one small cake.
Noun: parsimony. False friend: parsimonia in Spanish is slowness or calm.
A shortage of something — Escasez / falta.
There is a paucity of evidence.
Formal. Pattern: a paucity of something.
Sorry for what you did and wanting to make it right — Arrepentido/a.
Thinking deeply, often a little sadly — Pensativo/a / meditabundo/a.
She sat in a pensive mood.
Lying after swearing to tell the truth in court — Perjurio.
The witness was charged with perjury.
Read something carefully — Leer detenidamente / examinar.
He perused the contract before signing.
v|Noun: perusal. Often misused to mean skim; it means the opposite.
Calm and hard to excite — Flemático/a / impasible.
The goalkeeper stayed phlegmatic under pressure.
The ph sounds like f and the g is silent in phlegm.
Use someone else's words as your own — Plagiar.
Seeming reasonable or likely to be true — Plausible / verosímil.
The h is silent: POS-tyu-mus. Adverb: posthumously.
Developing ability earlier than usual — Precoz.
A precocious child of six reading Dickens.
A mixture of different things — Popurrí / miscelánea.
The concert was a potpourri of styles.
A bowl of dried scented petals — Popurrí.
There is potpourri on the shelf.
From French; the t is silent.
Keep putting off what you should do — Procrastinar / dejar para después.
I procrastinate whenever I have to write.
Say what will happen — Pronosticar / predecir.
Nobody can prognosticate the weather a month ahead.
A difficult situation where it is hard to decide — Dilema / aprieto.
I am in a quandary about the job offer.
Plural: quandaries. Phrase: in a quandary.
Extreme and unreasonable in opinion — Fanático/a / acérrimo/a.
He is a rabid supporter of the team.
A rabid fox was found in the wood.
An arranged meeting, or the place of it — Cita / punto de encuentro.
We agreed a rendezvous at the station.
From French; the z and the final s are silent. Same in the plural.
Officially cancel a law or decision — Rescindir / revocar.
Hopeful and confident about the future — Optimista / sanguíneo/a.
He is sanguine about next year.
Pattern: sanguine about something. From the old word for blood.
A comparison using like or as — Símil.
As brave as a lion is a simile.
Three syllables: SIM-i-lee. Compare metaphor, which makes no comparison word.
Person who doubts what others accept — Escéptico/a.
A spoken lie that damages someone's name — Calumnia / difamación.
He sued the paper for slander.
Say such a lie — Calumniar / difamar.
v|Slander is spoken; libel is written.
Happening now and then, not regularly — Esporádico/a / intermitente.
There was sporadic gunfire all night.
Only on the surface; not deep — Superficial.
He has a superficial knowledge of the subject.
Her taciturn husband nodded and left.
Short and to the point, sometimes rudely so — Escueto/a / lacónico/a.
Stop someone from doing what they planned — Frustrar / desbaratar.
Used so often it has lost its meaning — Trillado/a / manido/a.
The speech was full of trite phrases.
The novel describes a utopia with no money.
Keep changing your mind — Vacilar / titubear.
He vacillated between the two offers.
v|Noun: vacillation. Pattern: vacillate between things.
Using far more words than needed — Verboso/a / prolijo/a.
The report is accurate but verbose.
Noun: verbosity. Related: garrulous, terse is the opposite.
Show that someone was right or not guilty — Vindicar / reivindicar.
Likely to change suddenly — Volátil / inestable.
The market has been volatile all week.
